neighbours.label: historical colonial and church administration of communities (missions, protectorates, Indian bands, parishes with stipends and glebes): the governing of people by a colonial or ecclesiastical authority, versus modern civic or company administration
fire: In 1902 the mission station was handed over to the Anglican diocese and its school enlarged.
The colony was declared a British protectorate, and the paramount chief kept limited powers.
Pupils taken from the reserve attended the Methodist residential school until 1965.
The parish of Kilbride contains 1,840 inhabitants, and the living is in the gift of the bishop.
The Okanagan Indian Band petitioned the Crown over reserve boundaries in 1913.
Under the colonial administration, each district was governed by a native commissioner.
The vicar's tithe was commuted in 1838, and the glebe comprises 40 acres.
Missionaries founded a Catholic school for the Cree children of the settlement.
quiet: In 2002 the sports club was handed over to the town council and its gym enlarged.
The company was declared insolvent, and the chief executive kept limited powers.
Pupils from the suburb attended the new secondary school until it closed for repairs.
The village of Kilbride has a bakery, two pubs and a popular cycling club.
The local hiking club petitioned the council over parking near the trailhead.
Under the new management, each department was led by a regional director.
The gym's membership fee was raised in 2018, and the car park holds 40 cars.
Volunteers founded a coding club for the teenagers of the neighbourhood.
